prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: I keep B019 as a single-part prize and my position on the merits is unchanged: the chain from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect, through identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, to drugs with confirmed glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal effects is the most complete and best-confirmed on the shortlist, and no member disputes its maturity. Round 1 settled the first two names (all six hold Drucker and Holst). On the third name I stay with Mojsov, but I now hold that choice with a clearer rationale: the citation I propose rewards the physiology and the active form of the hormone, which is the discovery step that made both the biology and the later pharmacology tractable. Under that citation the three names are separable and defensible: Holst for human physiology of secretion and action, Mojsov for the active peptide, Drucker for proglucagon-derived peptide and receptor biology and translation.
statement.case_against: The weaknesses are credit and framing, not science. Habener is outside the supplied list and had major early contributions, Mojsov's priority is contested and none of us can verify it from the record, and a physiology citation leaves out Knudsen, whose acylated analogues became liraglutide and semaglutide. I have not changed my view that the prize should not hide this: if the committee wants to reward the therapy, that is better done openly than by swapping a name. A second part would not rescue it, because the three-person limit on the union of laureates would force dropping one of the GLP-1 names, which makes the main part weaker. I also concede that my Mojsov position depends partly on recollection of the priority history.

responses.point: Linnarsson holds Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating acylation and albumin binding as a discovery in its own right, while saying he would not block Mojsov under a purely physiological citation if the priority question is discussed openly.
responses.response: I have taken your argument seriously and I still disagree on the third name, but I move on one point: your demand that the priority question be discussed openly is right, and I state it here. My reading is that the evidence for Mojsov concerns identification and synthesis of the biologically active form, whereas Knudsen's contribution, decisive as it is for the drugs, starts from a defined peptide. Knudsen's work has no target without that step. The industrial setting is not my reason; I withdraw nothing from my round-1 point that where work was done does not decide whether it was a discovery. If diligence showed Mojsov's priority to be unfavourable, I would move to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen with a therapy-centred citation, and I accept that as a real condition on my vote, not a rhetorical one.

responses.point: Svenningsson proposes B019 with a citation on physiology and the active peptide, and in round 1 raised the question of whether a second part (B028 or B014) would be the stronger partner if the committee wants two achievements, noting that the three-person limit would force a split of the GLP-1 names.
responses.response: The chair's own constraint decides this for me. With at most three people in total, a second part means dropping at least one of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and every pair of GLP-1 names I can form is weaker than the trio because the physiology, the active peptide and the receptor biology are three distinct steps. I therefore withdraw the mild openness I expressed in round 1 to B028 as a companion part and now prefer B019 alone. B028 stays my first alternative because its credit (Walter and Mori) is the cleanest on the list, and I keep your point in mind that its therapeutic consequences are still emerging.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius supports the Drucker, Holst, Mojsov trio, would not discount Mojsov because credit is contested, and holds B014 first as an alternative, with June and Sadelain only and Rosenberg left out.
responses.response: I agree that a contested history calls for reading the primary record, not for omission, and that is how I treat Mojsov. On CAR-T I stay with June and Sadelain as the stronger pair, and your point that B014 shares the allocation problem with B019 persuades me to rank it second behind B028 as an alternative, not first: Eshhar's earlier chimeric receptor concept is not creditable under the supplied names, and I cannot settle Rosenberg without an arbitrary choice. I do part from you slightly on weight: B032 I would not place among my alternatives given your own point that it is a later validation of a formulated target concept.

responses.point: Perlmann would support Drucker, Holst and Knudsen if diligence on Mojsov's priority turned out unfavourable, and treats B028 as the cleaner two-person fallback if the GLP-1 attribution cannot be settled.
responses.response: I agree with the conditional structure of your position and adopt it for mine: Mojsov stays unless the priority record is adverse, and then the committee should move to a therapy-centred citation, not drop her silently. Where I differ is the fallback. If attribution were judged unresolvable I would first adjust the B019 names rather than abandon the prize, because a documented caveat on a prize this strong seems better than a clean prize on a weaker case, and I answer the chair's question on deferral that way. I accept that B028 is the cleaner fallback on credit if you and others disagree.

responses.point: El-Manira proposes the same trio and lists B016 (optogenetics) and B014 as alternatives, noting that long-term safety and outcome data are still accumulating and that Habener is not on the list.
responses.response: We agree on the configuration and on the caveat. On optogenetics I stay where I was: your argument that it is an exceptional tool is correct, but six claimants against three slots, and the unresolved line between channelrhodopsin discovery and neuronal application, keep it from being a candidate I can support this year, so I leave it out of my alternatives. On accumulating safety data I treat it as a reason to document the caveat in the citation discussion and not as a reason to defer.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener can be established from the record, which I cannot verify; this is the one fact that could change my third name.
Whether the committee would prefer a therapy-centred citation, in which case Knudsen replaces Mojsov and the Habener question remains.
Whether the omission of Habener is a defect serious enough to justify changing the configuration or deferral, or whether a documented caveat is sufficient, which I think it is.
Whether Eshhar's omission and the Rosenberg question can ever be settled for B014 if the committee later turns to it.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have published with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen and share Karolinska Institutet with several colleagues. None of this involves any credited name on the shortlist, and shared affiliation alone is not a recusal issue. I do not request recusal from any ballot.
